title: Light upon light
hook: His light is like a niche with a lamp in glass like a shining star, lit from a blessed olive (24:35)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last line of Al-Mu'minun, and your line was best of the merciful. Whose small mistake did you cover? Day four hundred ninety-two.

Before electricity, a house at night had one or two small lights, and people knew them intimately. A clay lamp with a wick floating in olive oil. A little hollow cut into the wall to set it in, so the draft wouldn't catch it and the plaster would throw the light back into the room. Glass, if you were lucky, to make the flame burn steady and bright. Surah An-Nur, the Light, takes that ordinary object, the lamp in the wall, and uses it to describe something nobody can describe. Today, the Verse of Light.

It begins with a sentence that is almost too large: "Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth." Then, straight away, it gets small. The likeness of His light is a niche, a mishkat, and in it a lamp. The lamp is in a glass. The glass is like a shining star. The lamp is lit from a blessed tree, an olive, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow on its own, even if no fire touched it. And then the phrase this day is named for: "Light upon light." Notice how the picture is built in layers. A niche holds a lamp. The lamp sits in glass. The glass shines like a star. The oil is nearly light already. Each layer gathers the light and makes it brighter, until the verse simply runs out of images and says it: light on top of light. The verse ends by saying God guides to His light whom He wills, and sets out likenesses for people. It doesn't pretend the picture is the thing itself. It's a likeness, a way in. Commentators have read the layers in many ways: the believer's heart as the niche, the Qur'an as the oil, the Prophet as the lamp. The theologian al-Ghazali wrote a book on this verse, called The Niche of Lights. And the olive neither of the east nor of the west? Some say a tree standing in the open, catching sun all day. Others say it points beyond every direction. The verse leaves it open.
screen: `THE LIGHT OF THE HEAVENS AND EARTH.` · `NICHE, LAMP, GLASS, STAR.` · `OIL THAT ALMOST GLOWS.` · `LIGHT UPON LIGHT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: light a lamp and look. If you can, switch on a small lamp or light a candle somewhere safe, and turn off the brighter lights around it. If not, look at whatever light is nearest, a window, a screen dimmed low. Watch how it falls on the wall behind it, how the wall gives some of it back. Let the layers add up. If you pray, you can say the verse's opening line quietly. The bell holds the time.
Light upon light. Nurun 'ala nur. The Verse of Light's picture of a niche, a lamp, a glass and an oil that almost shines by itself. Today's word.
Your line: light upon light. Tonight, when the lights come on, notice one lamp, and let it be a niche for a moment. Day four hundred ninety-two.

howItsDone: The Verse of Light, 24:35, is often recited and often appears in Islamic calligraphy; some medieval mosque lamps were inscribed with it.

match.prompt: the layers of the verse — tap the pairs.
pairs: neither of the east nor of the west

myth: the verse says God's light is exactly a lamp
it calls the lamp a likeness, a way in, not the thing itself.
in the verse, the oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it
each layer gathers the light, until it is light upon light.
commentators all agree on what the niche stands for
they read it many ways: the heart, the Prophet, the Qur'an.

fork.setup: you need to describe the light of God in a single verse. what do you reach for?
options: a small lamp in a wall niche, behind glass.
fork.reveal: the verse reaches for an ordinary household lamp, then layers niche, glass, star and oil until it says: light upon light.

original.note: Arabic: light upon light, from the Verse of Light, 24:35.

trapdoor: what you thought: a beautiful line about light.
what it means: a layered likeness, niche, lamp, glass, star, oil, each gathering light until it is light upon light.
what a scholar hears: mishkat is a non-through recess in a wall; the verse is ayat an-nur; al-Ghazali's Mishkat al-Anwar reads it as a map of levels of light.

sources.quoted: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth.

sources.ref: al-Ghazali, Mishkat al-Anwar (The Niche of Lights)
